_comment: Defaults for the 'Product Description' tab — the third tab, and the last one to get any
automation at all (WW-110). Until now NOTHING on it was filled: not one of its seven labels
existed in this repo, so `fill` reported all 90 known labels as 'belongs to another tab' and
the whole tab was typed by hand.
THE TAB HAS SEVEN FIELDS. Where each one comes from:
Model Number    – DERIVED in listing.ts from 'Seller SKU ID'. Same string; not repeated here.
Items Included  – DERIVED in listing.ts from the Description's 'WHAT YOU GET' block.
Quantity        – DERIVED in listing.ts from 'Weight', x1000. Vansh confirmed 2026-08-12
that the form's Quantity is the PACKED PARCEL in grams, which is the same
measurement the Inventory panel already computes. Deliberately NOT
defaulted: a listing whose parcel has never been weighed gets a BLANK box,
because a blank box is visible and a stale default weight is what WW-055
records reaching a live listing and costing money at settlement.
Type/Color/Size – below, shared by every balloon kit.
Size in Number  – below, and 8 IS THE ANSWER, not a placeholder waiting to be improved.
Vansh, 2026-08-12: 'the 10 inch foil we are folding, the 10 inch balloon
are not blown and then packed so they are small, so like that everything
almost mostly fits under 8-10 inches only.' THE TRAP THIS RECORDS: the
INVENTORY names materials by their INFLATED size ('10 INCH METALLIC
BALLOONS'), and nothing ships inflated — latex goes in flat, foil is
folded. So sourcing this field from the inventory, which looks like the
obviously correct fix and was proposed as one (C-052), describes a piece
that is not in the parcel. Same inflated-vs-flat distinction as WW-148,
which is still open for the size infographic — that picture wants the
INFLATED figure and this box wants the packed one. They are two different
numbers and neither is a correction of the other.
NOT FROM A SCAN. The seven labels were read off the live form by Vansh on 2026-08-12 and
typed in, because `npm run scan` has still never been run on this tab. Running it is still
worth doing — it is the only thing that can confirm each widget's KIND and each dropdown's
allowed values, and 'Decoration Kit' / 'Medium' below are the words he typed, not words we
have seen a dropdown offer. A value a dropdown does not offer is reported, never silently
typed (fields.ts lists what WAS on offer), so this is safe to run as-is.
NO LABEL HERE COLLIDES with the other two tabs — checked against all 90 captured labels.
'Type' is not 'Balloon Type', 'Color' is not 'Birthday Ribbon Color', and 'Size' is not any
of Width/Height/Depth. That check is not optional: loadProduct() merges every defaults file
into ONE flat map keyed by label, and the last time a label existed on two tabs it typed 8 cm
into one and 8 inches into the other (WW-123).
NO COMMAS inside any array value: Flipkart splits multi-value fields on ','.
_title: HOW FLIPKART BUILDS THE NAME BUYERS ACTUALLY SEE — measured off a live listing, 2026-08-12,
by comparing Vansh's form against his own product page. This is not a guess:
Color = Groom To Be Decoration | Mutlicolor Balloons | Sash & Foils   (entry order)
live   'PartyDreams Groom To Be Decoration, Mutlicolor Balloons, Sash & Foils Balloons'
NAME = <brand> + <Color values, comma-separated, IN ENTRY ORDER> + <Type>
The brand comes from the seller account. 'Model Name' is not part of it. The pill widget
lists newest at the TOP, which is why the form reads back-to-front against the title — the
order that matters is the order you typed, and that is the order the name uses.
CONSEQUENCE: Color and Type are the only two fields that write the product name, so they are
worth more than any other attribute on the form. It also means a typo there is a typo in the
name — the live listing above says 'Mutlicolor', so every buyer searching 'multicolor' misses
it. The cost of using Color this way is the colour FILTER, which these values make useless.
Vansh's call, 2026-08-12: worth it, because shoppers search words far more than they filter
_Quantity unit: The form's label is 'Quantity * (unit)' and the star is in the MIDDLE, which matters: label
matching strips a trailing star only, so a key of 'Quantity (unit)' would match nothing and
the picker would keep whatever it opened on. The key below is the label verbatim.
GRAMS, on Vansh's instruction 2026-09-03: 'fill Quantity 250 g, not kg, be careful.' The
number itself is derived in listing.ts as Weight x 1000, so 0.250 kg of parcel is 250 g here
— one measured fact, printed twice in the two units the form asks for.
